## Kestra Plugin Code Review

### Business Requirements: met
No linked issue. Both providers now forward it, and an unset value still falls back to the LangChain4j default. No scope creep: no build, dependency or CI changes.

review_comments.body:
🟡 [Guidelines] Reflection on a LangChain4j private field
Problem: `getDeclaredField("returnThinking")` + `setAccessible` reads an internal field of `OpenAiChatModel`, so the next LangChain4j bump can break this test by renaming the field. It also only checks that the flag is stored, not that the `thinking` output gets filled, and LangChain4j 1.22 reads reasoning only from the `reasoning_content` response field.
Fix: Prefer a WireMock test that stubs a chat completion response with reasoning for each provider (`baseUrl` pointing at the stub), runs the chat, and asserts `AiMessage.thinking()` (or the `thinking` output) is set when `returnThinking: true` and null otherwise. If you keep the reflection check, add a short note in the PR description saying it is test-only.

## QA report

**Edition**: OSS | **Docker tag**: v2.0.12-no-plugins
**Commit**: fa0e10259624 (head of this PR when tested)
**Result**: PASS, 6/6 scenarios, confidence 100%

Setup: shadow JAR built from the PR head (no tests run). OpenRouter and GitHubModels were pointed at a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that always returns `reasoning_content`. No real keys, no remote hosts. The mock shows the flag now reaches the model, not how a real provider behaves.

| Provider | `returnThinking: true` | `returnThinking: false` | unset |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenRouter | PASS: `outputs.chat.thinking` holds the mock text (new behaviour) | PASS: no `thinking` output | PASS: no `thinking` output |
| GitHubModels | PASS: `outputs.chat.thinking` holds the mock text (new behaviour) | PASS: no `thinking` output | PASS: no `thinking` output |

No errors in the logs. No HIGH or MEDIUM findings.

Note: whether real OpenRouter or GitHub Models return reasoning in `reasoning_content` (the only field LangChain4j reads) was not tested here.
Thanks @pcbeingused333 but what issue is linked to that PR?
